# Z Desk Queue — docs/QUEUE.md extract (evidence-bearing sections, 2026-11-05 revision)
Scope note: the entry-format spec section is omitted (non-claims-bearing). All other sections verbatim.

## Opening
Owner-approved 2026-11-02 ("make this into tooling you can do yourself"). The queue lets Z (or the owner) request consults with no per-consult approval ritual: enqueue an entry, a tick drains it, receipts auto-publish to the bus branch, and the entry moves to queue/done/ with a status marker. A tick is either the scheduled fire (*/10 * * * * cron in z-desk-queue.yml — never yet observed executing in the desk's receipts; honest residue C1/C2) or the owner's manual workflow_dispatch (the proven drain path; every completed drain to date).

## Processing
- Every 10 minutes the workflow runs the full test suite first, then drains up to MAX_PER_TICK (3) oldest queue/pending/ entries.
- Per entry it runs the same island.z_desk consult as the manual lane, so receipts land in runs/z-desk-queue-<run-id>-<n>/ on the bus: bus.jsonl, consult.md, report.md.
- The entry is then removed from queue/pending/ and a status marker is written to queue/done/<ts>-<n>.json with status in completed | error | parse-error. A held entry (future not_before) stays in queue/pending/ untouched — the hold is visible in the tick's Actions log.
- A failed entry is receipted and does not block the rest of the tick; a parse-error entry is moved to done without running.

## Checkout (library card)
Mark's design, 2026-11-03 — verbatim doctrine: "if the library is there they can check it out if it's not then they can't and they can report an error… any thinking or coordination would be done by the circle otherwise allowing dumb check out makes sense."
- Claim-before-run. A tick first CLAIMS each due entry with one commit moving it queue/pending/ → queue/claimed/; the push IS the atomic card swipe. Only then does it run the consult. Two workers (schedule + manual tick, or a future helper seat) can never run the same entry twice.
- Dumb on purpose. The checkout carries no priority logic, no leases, no expiry. Coordination, time windows, and who-should-run-what are the circle's common sense — the mechanism just makes collisions impossible.
- Claim collision = report, move on. If the claim push is rejected (another worker claimed first), the entry is receipted claimed-elsewhere and the tick proceeds. Neither worker bounces off the other's run.
- Held entries never steal claim slots. not_before holds and parse-errors are receipted before the claim step; only DUE entries count against MAX_PER_TICK.
- Containment (Astra pre-flight review, 2026-11-03): a claim-side crash still receipts every unreceipted due entry claim-failed — nothing silently vanishes; claim paths are stamped into the tick's status receipts BEFORE the bus switch (the bus branch carries no island/ code); only completed | error | parse-error may dequeue — any unknown status is left as-is; if the publish push stays rejected after retries the tick fails RED, and an always-on artifact upload preserves queue-status/, the receipts, and the claim log on every run.
- Statuses that own their bookkeeping: completed | error | parse-error → publish step removes the claim (and the pending entry on parse-error) and writes the done marker. held | claimed-elsewhere | claim-failed → the entry is left exactly where it is (claim-failed stays pending for a later tick).

## Kill switch
Disable the z-desk-queue.yml schedule (owner's click in the Actions UI). Pending entries then simply hold; nothing runs until it is re-enabled or a human fires a manual tick via workflow_dispatch.

## Cap distinctions + sprint-mode ceiling (rulings, 2026-11-03)
- Clamp vs. billing ceiling (Meraki, owner-endorsed): the per-entry cap is an input-side HARD CLAMP (clamped to QUEUE_CAP_USD); the spending stop is POST-CALL and soft (cap_kind: caller_declared_soft; the provider key cap governs actual billing). A clamped ceiling is not a hard billing ceiling.
- requested_by stays in the submission and is NOT copied into generated receipts; the submission → done-marker chain retains the credit link — deliberately, so post-mortems and retrospective analysis can trace who asked for what. (Meraki distinction, owner ruling 2026-11-03)
- SPRINT-MODE CEILING (owner, 2026-11-03): the normal ceiling stays $1. In declared sprint mode only, the ceiling may jump to $5 (maybe $10) for huge push builds (Puppy-class). Not the default; raise only in those circumstances. Implementation = a QUEUE_CAP_USD edit at sprint declaration, owner-gated.

## Correction (2026-11-05, owner-ordered)
The Nov-3 SECOND-CHECK consult (run z-desk-queue-41700028376-1, diff ISSUES_FOUND high) left two findings standing after R12 fixed the cap wording. Both fixed now by owner order ("address the audit note and fix it now", 2026-11-05):
1. "Without a human click per round" (opening paragraph) — overclaim, corrected. The scheduled tick has never once been observed executing; every completed drain to date was the owner's manual workflow_dispatch. The opening above is rewritten; no claim rides on the cron firing (C1/C2 stay open).
2. contains_secret docstring (island/z_desk.py) — ambiguous absolute, rewritten. "never proof a brief is secret-free" was grammatically mangled and readable as the scan guaranteeing secrecy. It now reads: best-effort scan over known token shapes; a clean result is not proof a brief is secret-free. Docstring-only change, zero behavior delta (next tick's test suite is the mechanical check).
